lab_title: Apparent Retrograde Motion: Exploring Mars' Loop from Earth and Beyond
top_level_objectives: Define apparent retrograde motion and identify the observational conditions under which Mars appears to reverse its motion in the sky.
Explain how the heliocentric model explains retrograde as a perspective effect due to the relative orbital motions of Earth and Mars.
Compare retrograde behavior among Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn and relate differences to orbital distance.
Use dual perspectives in AR: observe Mars from Earth and from an external heliocentric frame to build a coherent understanding of the phenomenon.
Develop data interpretation and scientific reasoning by predicting loop size and duration from orbital parameters and validating with AR visualizations.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 1 — Baseline Mars Motion from Earth
scenes.brief_purpose: Establish the baseline observational context: Mars drifts eastward against the background stars as seen from Earth. Set expectations for how the retrograde puzzle will emerge later. Audio cue: Narr_MarsBaseline_01
key_visuals: StarField.prefab with StarField_Texture_Dense
Planet_Earth.prefab with Earth_Texture_LightBlue (for perspective cues)
Planet_Mars.prefab with Mars_Texture_RedDust
Ecliptic overlay labeled with dates
Constellations overlay (text labels)
student_actions: Observe Mars’ slow eastward motion across consecutive nights; note its trajectory against the constellations.
Record a short note on the direction and approximate speed of Mars’ streaks across the sky.

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate how Mars appears to loop backward when viewed from Earth as Mars slows and temporarily reverses its motion. Audio cue: Narr_Retrograde_EarthView
key_visuals: Mars path shown as a colored trail on the starfield
Time-lapse controller to accelerate/decelerate sky progression
Labelled ‘Retrograde Loop’ indicating the loop segment
Textures: StarField_Texture_Dense, Constellation outlines
student_actions: Play the time-lapse to observe the onset, duration, and completion of Mars’ retrograde loop from Earth.
Sketch the looping path and describe in words what causes the loop in this Earth-centered perspective.

scenes.brief_purpose: Switch to an external viewpoint around the solar system to reveal two planets orbiting the Sun, showing that the loop is a perspective effect. Audio cue: Narr_Heliocentric_Perspective
key_visuals: Sun.prefab with Sun_Texture_Glow
Planet_Earth.prefab with Earth_Texture_LightBlue on a smaller inner orbit
Planet_Mars.prefab with Mars_Texture_RedDust on a larger outer orbit
Orbits colored by planet and with velocity arrows
Background: StarField_Texture_Sparse
student_actions: Move the camera to a location outside the Solar System and observe Earth and Mars moving in their respective heliocentric orbits.
Explain why the same phenomenon appears as a loop from Earth but as a smooth orbital motion in the heliocentric frame.

scenes.brief_purpose: Isolate the relative-motion mechanism by letting students adjust orbital speeds to see how the loop size depends on Earth’s speed relative to Mars. Audio cue: Narr_RelativeMotion_Scales
key_visuals: Two orbital paths: inner (Earth) and outer (Mars) with color-coding
Velocity vectors showing instantaneous motion
Slider controls: Earth orbital speed, Mars orbital speed
Labels: ‘Overtake’ and ‘Loop Size’
student_actions: Use the speed sliders to simulate faster/slower Earth or Mars motion and observe how retrograde loop size and duration change.
Describe the conditions that maximize or minimize the retrograde loop under your adjustments.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 5 — Jupiter and Saturn: Wider Perspective
scenes.brief_purpose: Compare Mars’ retrograde to Jupiter and Saturn, noting that larger orbital radii produce less dramatic loops. Audio cue: Narr_MarsJupiterSaturn_Comparison
key_visuals: Mars, Jupiter, Saturn on their respective heliocentric orbits
Relative motion arrows showing loop magnitudes
Scale: distances adjusted to reflect real orbital ratios
Textures: Jupiter_Texture_Band, Saturn_Texture_Rings, Mars_Texture_RedDust
student_actions: Observe the relative retrograde behavior of the three planets and articulate why Mars’ loop appears more pronounced.
Explain how orbital distance and orbital speed influence retrograde clarity.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 6 — Synthesis: From Epicycles to Orbits
scenes.brief_purpose: Integrate understanding by contrasting a geocentric epicycle explanation with the heliocentric interpretation, and summarize the learning. Audio cue: Narr_Synthesis_Comparative
key_visuals: Split-screen: left shows a geocentric epicycle demonstration (prefab: Epicycle_Demo) with Mars path
Right shows heliocentric explanation with Earth and Mars in their orbits
Text labels summarizing key points
Textures: StarField_Texture_Dense, Planet_Texture_Summary
student_actions: Compare both models and write a concise explanation of why the heliocentric view resolves the retrograde puzzle.
Identify evidence from the AR visuals that supports the heliocentric explanation and critique the epicycle approach.
